text:
sanjay: heads-up — the JS SDK dual-pkg publish just broke our edge sample app on the latest canary.

sanjay: reproduction: deploy sample to Cloudflare Workers (modules), import with `import { Redwood } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` and it throws "require is not defined" at runtime.

sanjay: locally the package.json has conditional exports like:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
but the built bundle still pulls the cjs path in the worker for some users.

kelly: hmm — are consumers using a bundler that resolves `main` instead of exports? we recently added a `main` field pointing to cjs to keep Node parity.

kelly: Cloudflare Workers honor the exports field for ESM but some bundlers (older esbuild versions) resolve package entrypoints differently.

jordan: another wrinkle: TypeScript lookup. we set top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" but some consumers that rely on `imports` path mapping don't get the `.d.ts` resolved for subpath imports. TS 4.7+ supports `types` under conditional exports but not all projects are on that.

jordan: TL;DR: two separate problems — runtime resolving wrong entry on edge (CJS bleeding into ESM env) and typings not being discoverable for some setups.

sanjay: quick patch idea:
- remove `main` (or point it at an ESM-compatible shim) so bundlers don't prefer CJS by default
- add explicit top-level `exports` fallback for edge: `"edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"` and a root-level `types` mapping
- publish a canary with `experimental.edge=true` tag for sample app testing

kelly: OK but removing `main` could break older Node LTS consumers expecting cjs. maybe we do a compatibility `main` -> cjs but use `exports` to force ESM for module-aware resolvers + add a publish step to add a separate `edge` tag.

ux-anna: from onboarding docs POV — this is high friction. new devs hit the sample app and see cryptic runtime errors. we should add a troubleshooting note in the quickstart and a clear "edge-compatible" example import line.

ci-bot: CI failed on integration: sdk-tests/edge-import-compat — https://ci.redwood/1234 (log snippet attached)

sanjay: logs show esbuild v0.17 in some users' tools resolves to `main` for package.json; upstream issues exist.

jordan: actionable plan:
1) open PR to adjust package.json: add explicit conditional types and an `edge` conditional export + remove ambiguous `main` reference (sanjay)
2) add a smoke test to ci: run sample app in a workers-like runtime with latest esbuild/browserify permutations (ci team)
3) update docs quickstart and add a note about node vs edge imports (ux-anna + kelly)
4) publish canary and ask a few customers to test (sanjay/kelsey)

sanjay: I'll draft the PR tonight. cc @kelly @jordan. If anyone has strong opinions on keeping `main` as cjs vs using an explicit `exports` fallback, speak up now.

kelly: fine with the PR as long as we include migration notes and keep a short-term compatibility lane (patch release).

jordan: agree. also add a unit test that asserts types are resolvable by tsc in a minimal project.

ux-anna: thanks — I'll update the quickstart after the canary is published so new signups don't hit this.

sanjay: thanks all — will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
